regions.label: Candle-lit table under the awning
regions.description: Two cloaked patrons, one hooded, at a candle-lit table under a red awning beside barrels and crates; a hanging lantern above.

visualQa.distinct: the only seated gathering in the source

regions.notes: Evidence is a hooded figure, a candle, barrels: a discreet conversation. It does not show a crime.

regions.label: Wet lane and arched passage
regions.description: A cloaked figure walks a wet cobbled lane toward a stone archway; a hanging lantern, barrels and a banner on either side.
regions.notes: A dark street is not a hideout: this crop supports "street at night" and nothing criminal.

catalog.note: The cloaked figure and the arch fill the strip: night street.

lists1.note: A 3.5:1 band over a tall region keeps a slice; the subject is cut away. The arch, which is the point, is lost.

lists2.note: Half-width tile keeps the lane but not the arch.

lists3.note: A third keeps the figure and a barrel, not the passage.

regions.label: Plotter's table
regions.description: A table with a parchment map under a red wax seal, a dagger, scattered coins, a silver goblet, bound books and a lit lantern.

visualQa.distinct: dagger + sealed map + coins, unlike V1 desk (no magnifier or scrolls)

catalog.note: A 1.7:1 region in a 1:2.6 strip keeps only the lantern or the goblet; the dagger and map are lost.

regions.label: Dagger-and-serpent banner
regions.description: A tattered maroon banner with a serpent coiled round a dagger.
regions.notes: An emblem, not a place. It says "a faction" but no environment is described by a banner, and a faction mark is not evidence of a criminal one.

regions.label: Lit city across the bridge
regions.description: A domed, lamp-lit city on a hill behind a stone viaduct under a night sky.
regions.notes: About 280x170 px in the master and soft: every frame would enlarge it. The setting is pleasant but belongs to no environment here.

regions.label: Saint statue and candle altar
regions.description: A robed stone statue holding a bowl of flame before a golden sun-halo, white sun banners, banks of candles on stepped altars, incense smoke.

visualQa.distinct: the only figure in the source

regions.notes: Specific iconography (a sun-halo and a flame bowl). It belongs to a faith with a Sacred Flame or a sun, not to every holy place.

catalog.note: Statue, halo and candles read in the strip.

lists1.note: A 3.5:1 band over a tall region keeps a slice; the subject is cut away. What survives is the rejected candle-steps crop.

lists2.note: Cuts the statue from the candles.

regions.label: Ivy arches over a mountain waterfall
regions.description: Tall Gothic arches and ivy-wrapped columns frame a misty valley with two waterfalls and a distant ruined archway on a crag.

visualQa.distinct: no statue, no candles: architecture and landscape only

regions.notes: Needs a human review. Beautiful and recognisable, but its only candidate (blade-root-sanctum) is contestable: the forest strip it would replace already shows the lore's deep green, and no other environment describes an open-air arcade over a valley. Not counted until a human decides.

catalog.note: Arch, ivy and waterfall in a vertical.

lists1.note: A 3.5:1 band over a tall region keeps a slice; the subject is cut away.

lists2.note: Loses the tower and the arch.

regions.label: Lotus pool in the cloister court
regions.description: A stone-rimmed reflecting pool with white lotus blossoms and lily pads on a polished court, flowers at the edge.
regions.notes: A 3.5:1 strip: it can only be a wide band (My Lists) or a square (Prep), never a Catalog strip.

catalog.note: A 3.5:1 region in a 1:2.6 strip keeps ~11 % of its width: a lotus fragment on water.

regions.label: Candle banks on the altar steps
regions.description: Rows of candles on stone altar plinths above a broad staircase, the statue only just cut off at the top.
regions.notes: A near duplicate of the statue crop: the same candles, the same steps, minus the one thing that makes it a place. Rejected under the "do not multiply crops of one statue" rule.

regions.label: Barred gate and torch-lit wall
regions.description: A heavy iron gate set in a stone arch over a dim cell with straw on the floor, hanging chains, a torch and a crossed-keys banner.
regions.notes: The cell (straw behind the bars) is what makes this a prison gate rather than just an iron gate.

catalog.note: Bars, chain and torch: a barred cell.

lists1.note: A 3.5:1 band over a tall region keeps a slice; the subject is cut away. Bars become a grille texture.

regions.label: Stair and arched bridge in the shafts of light
regions.description: A worn staircase climbs to a balustraded stone bridge over a vaulted arch, torches on the walls, mossy chains and light shafts from above.

catalog.note: Stairs, torch and the shaft of light.

lists1.note: A 3.5:1 band over a tall region keeps a slice; the subject is cut away.

regions.label: Explorer's kit on a stone ledge
regions.description: A lit lantern, an unrolled map, a compass, a pickaxe, coiled rope and a leather satchel on a ledge.

visualQa.distinct: close cousin of the V1 scholar's desk

regions.notes: Needs a human art review: a still life like V1's rejected dining table, but it names an activity (delving) that the archetype is about. Kept as "proposed": its mappings are not counted.

catalog.note: A 2:1 region in a strip keeps the lantern or the compass, never the kit.

lists3.note: A third tile keeps the lantern only.

regions.label: Flooded stone steps
regions.description: Broad rough-cut stone steps going down into dark still water; one candle burning on a lower step.
regions.notes: Generic wet stone: with the candle it hints at someone having passed, but nothing here names a place. Pixels are fine; meaning is not.

regions.label: Hanging gibbet cage
regions.description: An iron cage on a chain beside the arch.
regions.notes: About 160x320 px: an object, not a place, and too small for any frame.

mappings.reason: Lore: a gathering point a gang uses to shift goods, "often attached to a legitimate business". Cloaked men at a candle-lit table under a stall awning are exactly such a front; no gambling, goods or guards are shown.
The guildhouse of a settlement's organised crime: a building. This is an open-air table; nothing says guild.
A social spot "packed with seedy characters"; two patrons are not packed and nothing is seedy beyond the dim light (lighting alone is no evidence).
An ally was murdered; there is no body, clue or scene of a crime, only a conversation.
A secluded market in the sewers; this is an above-ground street awning. A dim stall is not an underground market.
A secret music club run by criminals; no band, no club, no bar.
A bustling post where supplies are sold or bartered; the crop is quiet and shows no goods.
Lore: merchants and patrons across classes; two cloaked drinkers in the dark do not make a bustling market.
A chase through the winding streets of a settlement: a wet lane, an archway and a hurrying cloaked figure are a fair stage; no pursuit is shown. The Catalog already shows a streets picture.
Lore: traffic, toxic smog and peddlers. The lane is quiet and clear.
A hidden or protected location to infiltrate; a passage at night is the road in, but no target is shown.
A chase along rooftops; the crop is street level.
A town under military occupation; no soldiers, no checkpoint.
A ramshackle slum of crumbling tenements and hovels; this is solid, lit masonry.
A universal scene about being chased in any terrain; nothing here is a pursuit.
Building the mystery, uncovering clues: a sealed map, a dagger, coins and a goblet are the evidence on an investigator's table. Reads as a plot rather than a crime scene, so Acceptable.
Lore feature "Prep Work": a map under a wax seal, a dagger and coins are the planning table of a job.
Casing a secure location: the map fits, but nothing says bank or vault.
Coins and a dagger suit "Trawling for Work", but a guildhouse is not shown.
Plausible back-room business, but the covert-table crop is the closer picture.
A majestic imperial domain; a candle-lit desk is the wrong scale.
A warded courtroom with witnesses; nothing judicial.
Coins and a goblet are not gambling; no tables, cards or dice.
A well-kept temple of healing and services: a candle-lit altar before a saint. The Catalog already wears this archetype picture, so no gain.
A divine power's stronghold propagating doctrine: statue, halo and banners fit. Already wears the archetype picture.
Lore: a chapel of beloved heroes of the Sacred Flame. The statue holds a bowl of fire. The lore is "moldering" and "puzzling doors", which this clean, lit chapel does not show.
Candles, incense and an altar fit, but the lore is an ancient Cathartoid, not a robed human statue.
A garden shrine; the crop is an interior altar with only a little ivy.
A verdant sanctum of flora and ancient stones: a robed, sun-haloed statue is faith-specific iconography that a wild sanctum does not carry.
A forest seat of wisdom, not a statue altar.
A holy site corrupted by darkness and madness; this is radiant and intact.
A Hierophant turning citizens into Jackalweres: a profane temple.
An encounter with a divine being in a divine realm, not a physical shrine.

Lore: a verdant sanctum of deep green flora and ancient stones. Ivy-wrapped arches fit the stones, but the crop is a pale, misty mountain valley, and the forest strip it would replace already carries the deep green. Gain is contestable, so it is not counted.
A bustling temple of healing and services; the vista has no altar, clergy or congregation.
An ancient seat of wisdom in the forest: no seat is shown.
A tranquil garden shrine: ivy and blossoms fit, but the lotus pool crop is the closer picture.
A burial mound on open grassland; this is built architecture.
A shrine encased in saltwater; nothing submerged.
A fey sanctuary around a great tree; built Gothic arches are not a tree sanctuary.
Lore: a tranquil garden shrine with a place of reflection. A lotus pool in a cloister court is that; no guardians or secrets are shown.
An outdoor swim at an extradimensional rift; a ceremonial pool is not a swimming place.
A grassland burial mound; no mound, no grass.
Lore: an extensive underground dungeon holding political prisoners. A barred gate over a cell with straw is a prison; the magic-resistant crystals are not shown.
A dim underground maze of chambers: a gate and torches fit. Already wears the archetype picture.
A subterranean fortress with a locked door: fits. Already wears the archetype picture.
Lava, steam and furnaces; nothing hot here.
An unstable floor above endless air; solid stone here.
A city of burning ash and iron bars in the Circles Below; a cold stone gate is not a damned city.
A machine workshop with bolted cells; this is masonry.
A tavern; the gate is a cell, not a bar.
Well-kept fortified tunnels with toll-keepers under a forest; this gate guards a cell.
Underground tunnels and chambers; fits. Already wears the archetype picture.
A subterranean fortress with something at the end; fits. Already wears the archetype picture.
A castle in disrepair covered in vines: the chains and moss fit, but the crop is clearly underground.
An ancient lost city underground: arches and stairs fit, but the environment is about a mind swap across ages.
A subterranean complex of echoing voices: nothing in the crop speaks of sound.
Tunnels carved into bedrock by miners; this is dressed masonry with a bridge.
Musty tunnels with bone piles under a city; no tombs.
A sealed library; no shelves.
A pickaxe, lantern, rope and map are the kit of a mining expedition; the mine itself is not shown.
A gold mine: a pickaxe fits, nothing says gold or haunted.
A search of a cursed city; map and lantern are generic searching tools.
A working magical-ore site with security; a lone kit is not an industrial mine.
A damp cave; a tidy ledge of gear is not a cave.

note: Experimental, unapproved for production. Mapping reviews are one reviewer's judgement; nothing here changes the archetype taxonomy or the artwork registry.
